signal: Apollo Funds minority investment closed; Alpine remains controlling owner. 75 brands, 46 states.
why_icp: Largest PE-backed home-services consolidator in the tracker. New capital usually means a push to grow the brands they already own, which is exactly what Arch sells.
suggested_contact_title: Head of Growth or VP Marketing (platform)
first_line: Saw Apollo close its minority investment in Apex on Oct 30, with Alpine still in control across 75 brands.

signal: PR: expanded in North Carolina (PE-backed HVAC/plumbing/electrical platform).
why_icp: Concentric-backed platform still adding markets. New geography is a moment they need a repeatable growth play, not another one-off campaign.
first_line: Congrats on the North Carolina expansion this fall. A new market is usually when local brand playbooks start to fray.

signal: Named add-on: Shipley Plumbing, Heating & Air Conditioning (Gryphon / NAEHS-backed).
why_icp: 15+ Southeast brands, still tucking in HVAC/plumbing/electrical shops. After a close, the platform has to make the new brand grow, not just rebrand it.
suggested_contact_title: Head of Partnerships or VP Growth
first_line: The Shipley add-on in August is a clean window to install one growth motion across the new Florida/Southeast brands.

signal: NEOH multi-brand Ohio platform add-on; also Live Free Heating in NH in Jun 2025. GS Alternatives-owned.
why_icp: 40+ Northeastern and Mid-Atlantic brands. A multi-brand Ohio platform is a density bet that only pays off if local marketing actually runs.
first_line: The NEOH Ohio platform you added this year only works if those brands can run campaigns without a central team doing it by hand.

signal: Blackstone announced agreement to acquire Champions Group. Tracker lists a Jan 2026 deal date.
why_icp: Blackstone-backed home-services platform. New sponsor usually tightens growth targets across the existing brands.
first_line: A Blackstone close is usually when brand-level growth stops being optional and starts showing up in the board pack.

signal: Bain Capital completed its acquisition of Service Logic; DealSeam also flags a Sep 2026 item.
why_icp: Commercial HVAC / mechanical platform under Bain + Mubadala. Different from residential roll-ups, still a multi-brand operator that needs a growth system after a sponsor change.
suggested_contact_title: Head of Sales or VP Marketing
first_line: Bain closing on Service Logic is the kind of ownership change that usually comes with a new growth target for the local brands.

signal: GI Partners launched a 2026 sale process (reported $3.5B+). Ownership may change. No buyer announced.
why_icp: 70+ centers in ~28 states. A live sale process is messy, but the next owner will be shopping for a growth operating system on day one.
suggested_contact_title: CMO or Head of Corporate Development
first_line: If the GI Partners sale process lands, the next owner inherits 70+ centers that still have to grow under new ownership.

signal: Watchtower Capital: Ally completed three add-on acquisitions in 2025, expanding its residential HVAC platform.
why_icp: Smaller PE platform still in add-on mode. Three recent tucks mean they now have to market as a group, not as three separate shops.
first_line: Three HVAC add-ons in a year is the moment the platform needs one campaign system, not three local vendors.

signal: Named add-on NJ Pipe Doctor (Apr 2025); 22+ brands across 19 states. Gridiron Capital.
why_icp: Multi-state HVAC/plumbing platform still publishing partner-brand growth. Good mid-size roll-up for a first Arch conversation.
first_line: NJ Pipe Doctor joining a 22-brand platform is the kind of tuck-in where local marketing usually lags the close by months.

signal: Altas Partners agreed to a majority investment, reported around $1.1B (May 2025). ~18 brands, $500M+ revenue.
why_icp: Fresh majority capital into an already large home-services platform. They will be asked to grow existing customers, not just buy more trucks.
first_line: A majority recap at this scale usually comes with a growth plan for the 18 partner brands, not just more M&A.

signal: TruArc Partners news item on Northwinds (May 2025). Rochester, NY platform.
why_icp: Regional PE-backed home-services platform. Smaller than Apex, closer to the operators Arch can actually get in a room.
first_line: A TruArc-backed regional platform is often still building its first shared growth function across the local brands.

signal: New Mountain Capital portfolio company; seven metros including NYC, Philly, Atlanta, DC.
why_icp: Multi-metro HVAC platform in Arch-relevant cities. Less of a dated 2026 close, more of a live PE-owned operator with several markets to run.
first_line: Seven metros under one PE owner is usually too many local vendors and not enough of a single growth system.
